deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics and no derivations. It is a historiographical note, page 9 (marked '(2' in the corner, archive folio 57), written in German Kurrent. It cannot be by Riemann: it refers in the third person to 'Riemann' and cites events of 1867 and 1871, after his death in July 1866. It is most likely an editor's or commentator's survey of the minimal-surface (Plateau problem) literature that followed Weierstrass and Riemann, perhaps connected with the Hattendorff edition of Riemann's posthumous memoir 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (1867/68), or a later lecture or essay.

Content, paraphrased:
(1) The general results obtained by Weierstrass on one side and Riemann on the other prompted the study of special cases.
(2) The first is H. A. Schwarz's prize essay, crowned by the Berlin Academy of Sciences in 1867. It was printed in 1871 as 'Bestimmung einer speciellen Minimalfläche', with a supplement (Nachtrag), an appendix (Anhang) and 6 plates of figures. Schwarz had already had a communication on this surface presented to the Berlin Academy (Monatsberichte, April 1865). The surface is bounded by a skew quadrilateral whose sides are four edges of a regular tetrahedron. The Nachtrag treats more general problems related to this one.
(3) The second is Arthur Schondorff's prize essay, crowned in 1867 by the Philosophical Faculty of the Georgia Augusta (Göttingen). Its title begins 'Über die Minimalfläche, deren Begrenzung von ...' and continues on the next, missing page.

There is nothing to reconstruct mathematically. The one geometric fact stated can be modelled as follows. Take a regular tetrahedron A=(1,1,1), B=(1,-1,-1), C=(-1,1,-1), D=(-1,-1,1). The closed polygon A-B-C-D-A uses four of the six edges, all of length 2*sqrt(2). Its vertices are not coplanar, so it is a genuinely skew quadrilateral (Schwarz's contour, giving the Schwarz D surface patch).
errors: No mathematical errors; the page contains no derivations.

Attribution issue: this page is not Riemann's own work. It is written after 1871 by another hand (it cites 1867 and 1871 and names Riemann in the third person), so it is posthumous editorial or historical material filed in the 'R.Minimal' bundle.

The historical claims match the standard record. Schwarz's Berlin prize essay was crowned in 1867 and published in 1871. His preliminary communication on the tetrahedral skew quadrilateral appeared in the Monatsberichte of 1865. Schondorff's Göttingen prize essay dates from 1867 (printed 1868).

results.what: Historical note: Schwarz's solution of the Plateau problem for the skew quadrilateral formed by four edges of a regular tetrahedron (Berlin prize 1867, printed 1871; preliminary note in Monatsberichte April 1865).
results.modern_name: Schwarz's minimal surface for a tetrahedral skew quadrilateral (fundamental patch of Schwarz's D surface); Plateau problem for polygonal contours

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a post-1871 bibliographic and historical summary by someone other than Riemann. It contains no mathematics and only well-documented facts about Schwarz's and Schondorff's prize essays.

checkable.asserts: The four sides of the quadrilateral A-B-C-D-A are edges of a regular tetrahedron of edge 2*sqrt(2).
The four vertices are not coplanar, so the boundary is a genuinely skew (räumliches) quadrilateral.
The two omitted tetrahedron edges (the diagonals AC and BD of the quadrilateral) have the same length, confirming regularity.
